story_clusters.headline: Trump-brokered 3-day Victory Day ceasefire collapses as both sides trade violation accusations
story_clusters.summary: US President Trump announced a three-day ceasefire (May 9–11) and 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner swap, which both Russia and Ukraine nominally accepted. Fighting continued throughout the period — no large-scale air strikes occurred but frontline combat persisted — with Kyiv and Moscow each blaming the other for violations. Zelensky said Russia was 'not even really trying' to observe the truce, while Russia's defense ministry claimed over 1,000 Ukrainian violations.

story_clusters.headline: Putin claims Ukraine war 'coming to an end,' expresses openness to meeting Zelensky in third country
story_clusters.summary: Speaking after Saturday's scaled-back Victory Day parade, Russian President Putin said he believed the conflict was drawing to a close and for the first time expressed willingness to meet Zelensky in a third country — conditional on a lasting peace deal being finalized. He also named ex-German Chancellor Schroeder as his preferred European mediator.

story_clusters.headline: Zelensky issues mock decree 'permitting' Moscow Victory Day parade with military coordinates included
story_clusters.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky signed a sardonic official decree on May 8 stating he was 'authorizing' Russia to hold its Victory Day parade on Red Square, while directing Ukrainian forces not to target that sector — and pointedly including the coordinates of Red Square. The gesture drew wide media attention as a piece of information warfare alongside the Trump-brokered ceasefire.

story_clusters.headline: Slovakia's Fico visits Putin in Moscow as diplomatic go-between; Kremlin disputes message delivery
story_clusters.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico traveled to Moscow for Victory Day, reportedly carrying a message from Zelensky indicating readiness for direct talks. The Kremlin subsequently stated that Fico had provided only an 'account' of his discussions with Zelensky rather than delivering formal messages. Fico later publicly said Putin expects Zelensky to initiate direct phone contact to demonstrate seriousness.

story_clusters.headline: Russia-Armenia row intensifies after Zelensky attends European Political Community summit in Yerevan
story_clusters.summary: Russia accused Armenia of providing Zelensky with 'a platform for anti-Russian remarks' at the European Political Community summit in Yerevan on May 4, summoning the Armenian ambassador. Armenian PM Pashinyan defended the hosting decision, stating Armenia 'is not an ally of Russia on Ukraine.' Russia's foreign ministry described Zelensky's remarks as 'terrorist threats' against Russia.

story_clusters.headline: Putin proposes ex-German Chancellor Schroeder as Ukraine mediator; Berlin dismisses idea
story_clusters.summary: Putin said on May 9 he would personally prefer longtime ally Gerhard Schroeder to serve as a European mediator for Ukraine peace talks. Berlin responded skeptically, with German government officials and commentators noting Schroeder's close ties to the Kremlin and his continued defense of Russia since 2022.

story_clusters.headline: Syrskyi frontline assessment: 106,000 Russian troops at Pokrovsk, Russia urgently expanding anti-drone forces
story_clusters.summary: Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Pokrovsk remains the most critical sector with approximately 106,000 Russian troops concentrated there. He also disclosed that Russia is urgently deploying four additional regiments, 24 battalions, and 162 batteries to counter Ukrainian strike drones, and plans to produce 7.3 million FPV drones in 2026. Syrskyi confirmed Ukrainian forces continue operations in Russia's Kursk region.

story_clusters.headline: Ukrainian drones diverted by Russian EW hit Latvian oil storage; Latvia's defense minister resigns
story_clusters.summary: Ukrainian drones that had been deliberately redirected by Russian electronic warfare systems struck oil storage facilities near Riga on May 8. Foreign Minister Sybiha confirmed the drones were Ukrainian and that Russian EW was responsible for the diversion, and Ukraine apologized to the Baltic states and Finland for similar incidents. Latvia's Defense Minister Andris Sprūds resigned on May 10 after the Latvian PM demanded his departure over the delayed air defense response.

story_clusters.headline: Budanov declares ceasefire extension conditional on Russian reciprocity; proposes unified foreign recruitment center
story_clusters.summary: Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov stated on May 5 that Ukraine would extend its unilateral ceasefire if Russia acted reciprocally, saying the next step was Moscow's. He subsequently published ceasefire condition statements as fighting continued. Separately, Budanov proposed the creation of a unified coordination center to streamline recruitment of foreign nationals into the Ukrainian armed forces.

story_clusters.headline: Svyrydenko announces EU-backed defense budget surge of UAH 1.56 trillion and privatization push
story_clusters.summary: Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko announced major budget amendments enabling a UAH 1.56 trillion increase in defense and security spending, funded by a €90 billion EU loan for 2026–2027. She also outlined Ukraine's 2026 privatization targets of approximately UAH 13 billion, including Sense Bank, Ukrgasbank, and Ocean Plaza, and reported that 25 companies had joined the private air defense initiative.

story_clusters.headline: Zelensky orders cabinet reshuffle, Energoatom governance overhaul, Sense Bank privatization
story_clusters.summary: Following a meeting with PM Svyrydenko, President Zelensky announced upcoming deputy minister-level changes in the Cabinet, directed the Energoatom supervisory board to initiate a new management board competition within a week, instructed acceleration of Sense Bank privatization by year-end, and ordered a competition for the head of the state forestry company Forests of Ukraine.

story_clusters.headline: SBU foils Russian-recruited assassination plot against Ukrainian Navy officer in Odesa ahead of May 9
story_clusters.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained a Russian-recruited agent in Odesa who had smuggled an AK-74 and planned to assassinate a senior Ukrainian Navy officer on May 9. A second SBU operation in Dnipro detained two suspects for planting a bomb under a Ukrainian soldier's car on May 7. The SBU also reported 596 Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure since the start of the full-scale war.

story_clusters.headline: SBU strikes Russian refineries repeatedly; Zelensky confirms 'Flamingo' cruise missile use on deep targets
story_clusters.summary: Ukraine's Security Service confirmed multiple drone strikes on Russia's Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez refinery in Perm — the third such strike in nine days — targeting facilities approximately 1,500 km from Ukraine. President Zelensky also confirmed that Ukraine used 'Flamingo' long-range cruise missiles to strike a military-industrial plant in Cheboksary producing navy components.

story_clusters.headline: Zelensky orders PMC legalization legislation; Defense Minister Fedorov deploys AI anti-drone turrets and seeks Swedish Gripen jets

story_clusters.headline: Ukraine-Norway joint 155mm artillery shell production agreement announced

story_clusters.headline: Hungary returns Oschadbank assets; Zelensky congratulates new PM Magyar on taking office
